name: Europe hybrid attacks
value: Denmark blames Russia for foiled murder plot
summary: Denmark says Russian intelligence planned a foiled plot to kill a Ukrainian rapper; it expels Russia's attaché
state: Denmark's security service PET said on 20 Nov that Russian intelligence planned and initiated a plot to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner before a concert on 25 Sep; two Danish men linked to a criminal gang are charged and in custody, and Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attaché (Euronews; CNN). Russia's embassy said the accusations lacked proof. Estonia blames Russian military intelligence for a foiled arson at a drone maker in mid-November. No sabotage causing casualties or a major outage was found to 21 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: State-linked plots in Europe increasingly use hired criminals. Anyone offered cash for unusual tasks, such as filming sites or moving packages, can report it to the police.
rubric_hit: Watch: plot attributed to a state (Denmark's PET, 20 Nov); no casualties or major outage

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
